hints: Focus on what free radical substitution of methane can actually build, including the normal chlorinated methanes and what happens in termination steps.
Remember that $\text{CH}_3\cdot$ radicals can join together in termination to give a trace of ethane, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$, and $\text{Cl}\cdot$ radicals can rejoin to give $\text{Cl}_2$.
Check each list for a formula that cannot fit, especially any 2-carbon compound that is unsaturated or too highly chlorinated to come from just $\text{CH}_4 + \text{Cl}_2$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the normal substitution products**

Methane undergoes successive substitution to give chloromethane, dichloromethane, trichloromethane and tetrachloromethane. Think of replacing H by Cl one at a time.

$$\text{CH}_4 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CHCl}_3 \rightarrow \text{CCl}_4$$

**Remember the termination products**

Propagation makes $\text{CH}_3\cdot$ and $\text{Cl}\cdot$ radicals. In termination these radicals can combine in any pair.

$$\text{CH}_3\cdot + \text{CH}_3\cdot \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6$$
$$\text{Cl}\cdot + \text{Cl}\cdot \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2$$
$$\text{CH}_3\cdot + \text{Cl}\cdot \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$$

**Spot the impossible compound**

So $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{CHCl}_3$, $\text{CCl}_4$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ and even reformed $\text{Cl}_2$ can all be found in the mixture. A compound like $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_2$ has formula of an unsaturated dichloroethene, with a C=C double bond. Free radical substitution only makes saturated single-bonded products, so this cannot be made.

options.A: All three can be made. $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and $\text{CCl}_4$ are normal propagation products, and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ is made in small amount by termination between two methyl radicals.
options.B: All three can be present as made species. $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{CCl}_4$ are normal products, and $\text{Cl}_2$ is reformed in the termination step $\text{Cl}\cdot + \text{Cl}\cdot \rightarrow \text{Cl}_2$.
options.C: All three are the classic successive chlorination products of methane: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{CHCl}_3$. This list contains only expected products.
options.D: $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$ and $\text{CHCl}_3$ are normal products, but $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2\text{Cl}_2$ is not made. It is unsaturated and cannot arise from free radical substitution of methane, which gives only saturated chloromethanes plus trace saturated $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$.
